full_judgment:
4. The defendant No. 1 resisted the suit upon two grounds firstly that the plaintiff having failed to tender the consideration money within the stipulated time that is within 10 years he was not entitled to get re-conveyance and secondly that the suit having been filed beyond three years from the due date of re-conveyance was barred by limitation. The learned Munsif accepted both the defence pleas and dismissed the suit. On appeal the learned Subordinate Judge found in consideration of evidence that the consideration was duly tendered within the specific time that is within 10 years of the kabala This being a finding of fact based on evidence there is no scope to re-assess this point which has been concluded by the finding of the appellate court. 

 5. On the other point that is point of limitation the learned Subordinate Judge found that since the plaintiff was conducting a proceeding before the Circle Officer over the same matter so that period will have to be excluded under section 14 of the limitation act and accordingly the suit was within time. So he reversed the order of the learned Munsif and decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiff. 

 6. On behalf of the defendant respondent that is on behalf of the present petitioner it has been submitted that the learned Subordinate Judge made a miscalculation about the period which was actually covered by the proceeding before circle Officer. It was contended that only 55 days were covered by the proceeding before the Circle Officer and even if these 55 days are excluded or condoned under section 14 of the Limitation Act still then the suit is barred by limitation. In this case there is no dispute that the kabala was executed on 28.2.62 and the defendant’s agreement was also of the same date wherein it was agreed that the re-conveyance shall be made on return of consideration within 10 years that is within 28.2.72. According to Article 113 of the Limitation Act the period of limitation for this suit was three years from 28.2.72 that is the suit was required to be filed within 28.2.75. But in this case the suit has been filed on 11.5.76 that is one year and three months after the period of limitation had expired. It is in evidence that the present plain-tiffs brought a petition before a Circle Officer for having the re-conveyance on 8.4.74 and Ext. 2(b) shows that the Circle Officer ordered deli-very of possession on 22.6.74 so only this period from 8.4.74 to 22.6.74 that is about 55 days could be condoned under section 14 of the Limitation Act. The learned Subordinate Judge also held that only the period of the proceeding before the Circle Officer could be condoned but he took a wrong date namely 22.6.76 as the date of order of delivery of possession which was a clear mistake according to Ext. 2(b). Now even if the period covered by the proceeding started by the plaintiff before the Circle Officer is condoned under section 14 of the Limitation Act that gives a condonation of only 55 days that is less than two months while in this case the delay has been for one year and three months. 

 7. On behalf of the O.Ps. Mr. Khondaker Saiful Hoque, submitted that since the defendant had brought a suit for declaring the order of the Circle Officer passed under P.O. 88 of 1972 in favour of the plaintiff as illegal so a further period covered by that suit should also be condoned under section 14. This submission is not acceptable in law. It is only when the plaintiff bonafide conducts another proceeding over the same subject matter that the period covered by such proceeding can be condoned under section 14 of the limitation act but an independent proceeding which the adverse party namely the defendant conducts can not be a matter for consideration for condoning the delay in filing the suit by the plaintiff under section 14 of the limitation act. 

 8. The result is that the suit was barred by limitation as was rightly held by the learned Munsif and it was a mistake of law made by the learned Subordinate Judge in finding the suit not to be barred by limitation.
